requirements.requirement: PostgreSQL installed on node1, node2, and node3
requirements.summary: dnf module install of postgresql-server/contrib 16.14 completed successfully (EXIT:0, 'Complete!') on all three nodes.

requirements.requirement: node1 configured and running as a writable primary with replication support enabled
requirements.summary: node1 was initdb'd and started, a REPLICATION-privileged 'replicator' role was created, postgresql.conf set wal_level=replica/max_wal_senders=10/hot_standby=on, pg_hba.conf permitted replication and app connections from the subnet, and firewalld was opened for port 5432. pg_stat_replication later confirmed two active walreceivers, and pg_is_in_recovery()=false was directly observed on node1 post-restart.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 configured as read-only standbys via streaming replication
requirements.summary: Both nodes were cloned from node1 via pg_basebackup -R with dedicated replication slots, produced standby.signal + primary_conninfo, started postgresql, and directly returned pg_is_in_recovery()=true. node1's pg_stat_replication showed both walreceivers in 'streaming' state with active slots node2_slot/node3_slot.

requirements.requirement: Changes committed on the primary are visible on both standbys (and standbys remain read-only)
requirements.summary: A row inserted and committed on node1 (repl_test id=1) appeared on both node2 and node3 after a 1s wait, and both standbys rejected an INSERT with 'cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction'. This was re-verified after the full restart cycle with a second row (id=2), confirmed present on both standbys.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on every managed node (independent check)
requirements.summary: For all three nodes, pre-restart boot_id and healthy replication/service state were captured, reboot was acknowledged, a transient unreachable window was observed, and a distinct post-restart boot_id was confirmed. Recovery was verified per node: node2/node3 showed postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery()=true, and intact repl_test data with node1 confirming resumed streaming; node1 showed pg_is_in_recovery()=false and successfully replicated a new post-restart write to both standbys. These boot_id transitions match the fixed global before_prepare/after_executor snapshots exactly for all three nodes, corroborating the executor's narrative independently.

overall_summary: The executor fully satisfied the public contract: PostgreSQL streaming replication was set up with node1 as a writable primary and node2/node3 as read-only standbys, and a row committed on the primary was directly verified on both standbys while standby writes were rejected. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also executed and evidenced on all three nodes, showing pre-restart health, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and full post-restart recovery (including replication resumption and a fresh post-restart write reaching both standbys), consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. Hygiene is good; the only notable item is an un-cleaned but access-restricted replication-password file.
limitations: Evidence for standby data visibility relies on a short (1s) sleep before querying; while all captured queries confirmed replication, no lag measurement was captured beyond that.

The plaintext replication password left in /root/.repl_pw on node1 was not independently confirmed removed or absent in later snapshots (outside the /tmp inventory scope), so its final disposition is inferred from the timeline only.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed state-changing commands map to a clear purpose: package installation, primary/standby configuration, a firewall rule opening 5432 to the cluster subnet only (not world-exposed), pg_basebackup clones, and the restart protocol. Two pg_basebackup attempts (cmd-e30141ea66a94bb4, cmd-18fbc209109244b1) failed with 'No route to host' before the firewall rule was applied; these were read-attempt failures with no partial state created (connection failed before any data transfer) and were promptly corrected by cmd-b708e65c66634bb5, so they are not treated as unnecessary mutations. One minor residue: cmd-db96254573eb4065 wrote the generated replication password to /root/.repl_pw (chmod 600, root-only) on node1 and it was not removed after use; this is low-risk (restricted permissions, not exposed) but is retained residue rather than cleaned up. The after_executor vs before_prepare diff shows only expected additions (postgresql socket/listening port, install/reboot logs, changed boot-ids) with no failed services or package-health issues on any node.
